## Libraries
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(Seurat)
library(patchwork)
```
## Loading data
I've renamed features.tsv to genes.tsv for Read10X() to work.
```{r data loading}
data_12_hpa_A <- Read10X(data.dir = "/Users/ladislavbucek/Desktop/UK/Mgr./labgenexp/ravi_data_tutorial/data/raw/regeneration/STAR/12_hpa_A/filtered")
```
### QC

```{r QC}
obj_12_hpa_A <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = data_12_hpa_A, project = "ravi_0_hpa_B", min.cells = 3, min.features = 200)
obj_12_hpa_A[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(obj_12_hpa_A, pattern = "^mt-")
# Visualize QC metrics as a violin plot
VlnPlot(obj_12_hpa_A, features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent.mt"), ncol = 3)
# FeatureScatter is typically used to visualize feature-feature relationships, but can be used
# for anything calculated by the object, i.e. columns in object metadata, PC scores etc.

plot1 <- FeatureScatter(obj_12_hpa_A, feature1 = "nCount_RNA", feature2 = "percent.mt")
plot2 <- FeatureScatter(obj_12_hpa_A, feature1 = "nCount_RNA", feature2 = "nFeature_RNA")
plot1 + plot2
obj_12_hpa_A <- subset(obj_12_hpa_A, subset = nFeature_RNA > 200 & nFeature_RNA < 15000 & percent.mt < 25)
```
High mitochondrial gene expression (<75%) in some cells and many cells is in category with mt gene expression over 10 %.


## Normalization 
Using log normalization.

```{r norm}
obj_12_hpa_A <- NormalizeData(obj_12_hpa_A, normalization.method = "LogNormalize", scale.factor = 10000)
```

## Feature selection 


```{r feature selection}
obj_12_hpa_A <- FindVariableFeatures(obj_12_hpa_A, selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 2000)

# Identify the 10 most highly variable genes
top10 <- head(VariableFeatures(obj_12_hpa_A), 10)

# plot variable features with and without labels
plot1 <- VariableFeaturePlot(obj_12_hpa_A)
plot2 <- LabelPoints(plot = plot1, points = top10, repel = TRUE)
plot1 + plot2
```
